title: Βάτραχοι ⟨γείτονες⟩
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 67 (= Perry 69). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.l: Two frogs were neighbours to one another.
sentences.n: Chambry's Greek title reads Βάτραχοι ⟨γείτονες⟩: the angle brackets are his mark for words he supplies himself, square brackets for words he judges later additions and deletes. The text is a reconstruction, and the edition says so on its face.

sentences.t: Ἐνέμοντο δὲ ὁ μὲν βαθεῖαν καὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ πόρρω λίμνην, ὁ δὲ ἐν ὁδῷ μικρὸν ὕδωρ ἔχων.
sentences.tr: Enemonto de ho men batheian kai tēs hodou porrō limnēn, ho de en hodōi mikron hydōr echōn.
sentences.l: And the one inhabited a deep pond far from the road, the other, in the road, having a little water.
sentences.i: One of them lived in a deep pond well away from the road, the other in the road itself, with only a little water.
sentences.n: μέν … δέ splitting a pair — 'the one… the other…' — the commonest sentence-shape in these fables. ἐνέμοντο is the middle of νέμω, 'to have as one's pasture', hence simply 'they dwelt in'.

sentences.t: Καὶ δὴ τοῦ ἐν τῇ λίμνῃ παραινοῦντος θατέρῳ μεταβῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν, ἵνα καὶ ἀμείνονος καὶ ἀσφαλεστέρας διαίτης μεταλάβῃ, ἐκεῖνος οὐκ ἐπείθετο λέγων δυσαποσπάστως ἔχειν τῆς τοῦ τόπου συνηθείας, ἕως οὗ συνέβη ἅμαξαν τῇδε παριοῦσαν θλᾶσαι αὐτόν.
sentences.tr: Kai dē tou en tēi limnēi parainountos thaterōi metabēnai pros auton, hina kai ameinonos kai asphalesteras diaitēs metalabēi, ekeinos ouk epeitheto legōn dysapospastōs echein tēs tou topou synētheias, heōs hou synebē hamaxan tēide pariousan thlasai auton.
sentences.l: And so, the one in the pond urging the other to move across to him, so that he might share in both a better and a safer way of living, that one would not be persuaded, saying that he was hard to drag away from his familiarity with the place, until it came about that a wagon passing that way crushed him.
sentences.i: And when the one in the pond urged the other to come across to him, so as to share a better and safer life, the other would not be persuaded: he said he was hard to prise away from the place he was used to — until a wagon came by that way and crushed him.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute (τοῦ … παραινοῦντος) sets the frame before the main clause arrives. δυσαποσπάστως ἔχειν: ἔχω with an adverb stands for 'to be' in that state — 'to be hard to tear away' — with the genitive of what he cannot be torn from. ἕως οὗ, 'until'.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ τοῖς φαύλοις ἐπιτηδεύμασιν ἐνδιατρίβοντες φθάνουσιν ἀπολλύμενοι πρὶν ἢ ἐπὶ τὰ καλλίονα τρέπεσθαι.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn anthrōpōn hoi tois phaulois epitēdeumasin endiatribontes phthanousin apollymenoi prin ē epi ta kalliona trepesthai.
sentences.l: So too those among men who linger in worthless pursuits perish first, before turning to better things.
sentences.i: So too those men who spend their lives in worthless pursuits are destroyed before ever they turn to anything better.
sentences.n: φθάνουσιν ἀπολλύμενοι is the mirror of λανθάνω with a participle: the main idea ('first, before anything else') sits in the verb and the action in the participle, so 'they perish before they can…'. πρὶν ἤ with the infinitive, 'before'.
